note: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts predicted vemurafenib's pathway blockade, exposure threshold and tumour regression in the phase 1, and the paradoxical-activation model explained the cutaneous squamous-cell carcinomas and their RAS genotype.
label: Melanoma (BRAF)

engagement.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
engagement.note: PLX4720 suppressed ERK phosphorylation only in BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts; no patient biopsy comparison yet.
engagement.short: pERK blocked only in V600E cells
engagement.quote: Consistent with the high degree of selectivity, ERK phosphorylation is potently inhibited by PLX4720 in B-Raf(V600E)-bearing tumor cell lines but not in cells lacking oncogenic B-Raf.

engagement.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
engagement.note: Paired phase-1 biopsies: responders showed >80% pERK inhibition, the broad blockade xenografts had required for regression.
engagement.quote: At higher drug exposures afforded by a new amorphous drug formulation, greater than 80% inhibition of ERK phosphorylation in the tumours of patients correlated with clinical response.
engagement.judgement: One paper (Plexxikon/Roche authors) holds both sides: xenograft pathway blockade and regression versus paired pre/on-treatment patient biopsies (NCT00405587, PLX06-02). The model-side pERK threshold is not stated numerically, so magnitude is direction-only. Full text read via the PMC author manuscript (PMC2948082).

dose.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
dose.note: Oral PLX4720 regressed V600E xenografts at exposures later used to set the clinical AUC target; no patient data yet.
dose.quote: In B-Raf(V600E)-dependent tumor xenograft models, orally dosed PLX4720 causes significant tumor growth delays, including tumor regressions, without evidence of toxicity.

dose.note: Colo205 xenografts set a regression threshold (AUC >300-400 uM.h); patient regressions began once doses exceeded it.
dose.short: Patient regressions began above xenograft AUC
dose.quote: Consistent with nonclinical findings, tumor regressions in PLX06-02 were first observed in the dose range of 240 mg b.i.d. to 360 mg b.i.d. that on average exceeded the target exposure threshold AUC0-24h of 400 µM*hr.
dose.reason: Xenograft AUC threshold held in patients
dose.judgement: Dated to the FDA review (NDA 202429) because its sentence states the comparison in one line and documents the filed models (LOX, Colo829, A375 xenografts; Colo205 exposure titration). Bollag 2010 (doi:10.1038/nature09454) had already published the same comparison: Colo205 regressions at AUC0-24 ~300 uM.h, and phase-1 partial responses in BRAF-mutant patients once AUC0-24 exceeded 300 uM.h; re-score the year to 2010 if first publication is preferred. The 960 mg BID dose (AUC 1741 uM.h) sits well above the threshold, but the threshold itself held, hence within_2x.

efficacy.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
efficacy.note: PLX4720 regressed BRAF V600E xenografts and spared BRAF-wild-type cells; the vemurafenib product repeated this in A375, Colo829 and LOX.
efficacy.quote: In B-Raf(V600E)-dependent tumor xenograft models, orally dosed PLX4720 causes significant tumor growth delays, including tumor regressions, without evidence of toxicity.
efficacy.judgement: Vemurafenib itself was profiled in A375, Colo829 and LOX xenografts in Yang 2010 (doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-10-0646), the models named in the FDA pharmacology review.

efficacy.model: BRAF V600E cell lines and xenografts
efficacy.note: Xenografts regressed and 26 of 32 phase-1 patients at 960 mg BID responded; BRAF-wild-type patients did not.
efficacy.quote: Indeed, the Phase 1 clinical data revealed a remarkably high 81% response rate in metastatic melanoma patients treated at an oral dose of 960 mg twice daily.
efficacy.judgement: Same paper reports xenograft regression and the phase-1 response (NCT00405587; Flaherty 2010, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1002011, is the trial report). Resistance also matched: PLX4032-resistant sublines (NRAS Q61K, PDGFRB; Nazarian 2010, doi:10.1038/nature09626) and an ORF screen (COT/MAP3K8; Johannessen 2010, doi:10.1038/nature09627) found the same mechanisms in patient relapse biopsies. No BRAF inhibitor in this context was flagged by the model and then failed, so no `neg`. Sorafenib (BAY43-9006), which delayed melanoma xenografts in Karasarides 2004 (doi:10.1038/sj.onc.1207785) and failed in melanoma, is treated as a multi-kinase class, not this one; scoring it here would make the cell `contra`. Dabrafenib later repeated the pattern (BREAK-3, Hauschild 2012, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(12)60868-X). Magnitude is direction-only because xenograft regression and RECIST response rate are different metrics.

safety.model: BRAF V600E xenografts; rat and dog toxicology
safety.note: V600E xenografts and rat/dog toxicology carried no RAS-mutant skin and were silent on cutaneous SCC.
safety.quote: In B-Raf(V600E)-dependent tumor xenograft models, orally dosed PLX4720 causes significant tumor growth delays, including tumor regressions, without evidence of toxicity.
safety.judgement: Silence, not a prediction: the FDA pharmacology review's toxicity correlation table lists cutaneous SCC at ~29% of patients with no finding in rats or dogs.

safety.model: BRAF-wild-type / RAS-mutant cells and xenografts (paradoxical RAF activation)
safety.note: RAF-dimer transactivation in RAS-mutant cells predicted MEK/ERK-driven toxicity; keratoacanthoma-type SCC in 31% of phase-1 patients matched.
safety.quote: These predictions have been borne out in a recent clinical trial of the RAF inhibitor PLX4032 (refs 4, 5).
safety.judgement: The cuSCC were seen in patients (phase 1, 2009; Flaherty 2010 reports 10 of 32 extension-cohort patients) before the paradox papers (Heidorn Jan 2010, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2009.12.040; Hatzivassiliou, doi:10.1038/nature08833; Poulikakos), so the 2010 agreement is explanatory rather than a forward prediction; abstract-level for Poulikakos. The forward predictions were then tested and held: 60% (21/35) of patient cuSCC/keratoacanthomas carried RAS (mostly HRAS Q61L) mutations, and PLX4720 accelerated HRAS-mutant lesions in DMBA/TPA mice, blocked by a MEK inhibitor (Su 2012, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1105358; trials NCT00405587, NCT00949702 results posted 2011-12-22, NCT01001299 2015-10-05, NCT01006980 2011-11-16); adding trametinib to dabrafenib cut cuSCC from 19% to 7% (Flaherty 2012, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1210093; NCT01072175, results posted 2013-11-21). The FDA pharmacology review credits the model ('Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma ~29% ... Modeled in Athymic Mice') from sponsor A431 cuSCC xenograft studies, so model_filed is true. A stricter reading scores the standard package as `contra` (tox species missed a 20-30% toxicity); I scored the paradox model because it is the model the class relied on for this question.
